question: to the Commission Galato Alexandraki (ECR) Subject:
Zervochia, South Pelion: restoration after Storm Daniel, Natura 2000 and legal action against residents

In the village of Zervochia in South Pelion, Greece, there are reports that following damage caused by Storm Daniel in 2023, collapsed stream crossings remain provisionally filled in, old, dilapidated bridges make it dangerous for fire engines to pass, while rural roads and main access routes remain in poor condition even after water supply works were carried out in 2024. Residents, including the elderly, are reportedly forced to take matters into their own hands to restore the basic functioning of roads, calling for safe access, property protection, water and fire safety. At the same time, the Municipal Council of South Pelion reportedly decided on 7 May 2026 to take legal action against residents who protested publicly. What is more, questions have been raised about photovoltaic installations in an area connected to the Pelion Natura 2000 protected area (GR1430008), following a court decision for the annulment of a permit. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Will the Commission request data on the use of EU funds for the restoration of infrastructure following Storm Daniel in the municipality of South Pelion?
Will it examine compliance with Natura 2000 rules and Directive 92/43/EEC in the Zervochia area?
With regard to public participation in environmental matters, what is its view on legal action against residents who report safety, access and environmental protection problems?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) 1. In 2024, Greece received EUR 101 million of assistance from the EU Solidarity Fund1 for the disaster caused by storm Daniel in November 2023. The Greek Cohesion Policy programmes integrated emergency relief in Greece’s disaster management system to aid households as well as to support workers and firms with job retention subsidies and business reactivation measures. Greece’s Recovery and Resilience Plan2 supports the restoration of Thessaly’s road and railway network. The Commission will assess how EU funds contributed to the recovery efforts based on the evidence which the Greek authorities will provide. 2. According to Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive3, any plan or project likely to have a negative effect on a Natura 2000 site4 must undergo an impact assessment and can only be approved if they do not compromise the site’s integrity. Exceptions to this obligation may be accepted under the conditions established in Article 6(4) of the Directive. It is primarily Greece’s responsibility to ensure compliance with EU environmental law. 3. Article 3(8) of the Aarhus Convention5, of which the EU and its Member States are party to, requires parties to protect environmental defenders when they make use of their rights, including public participation. The EU partially implements this obligation through Directive (EU) 2024/10696, the transposition period of which expired on 7 May 2026. The Commission will follow up with the Greek authorities on the correct transposition.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002 of 11 November 2002 establishing the European Union Solidarity

Fund (OJ L 311, 14.11.2002, p. 3) as amended by Regulation (EU) No 661/2014 of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014 (OJ L 189, 27.6.2014, p. 143) and by Regulation (EU) 2020/461 of the European Parliament and the Council of 30 March 2020 (OJ L 99, 31.3.2020, p. 9): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:32002R2012. 2 https://reforms-investments.ec.europa.eu/recovery-and-resilience-facility-1/country-pages/greeces-recoveryand-resilience-plan_en?prefLang=es. 3 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7. 4 Either individually or in combination with other plans or projects. 5 Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-Making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters, 25 June 1998: https://unece.org/environment-policy/public-participation/aarhusconvention/text. 6 Directive (EU) 2024/1069 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on protecting persons who engage in public participation from manifestly unfounded claims or abusive court proceedings (‘Strategic lawsuits against public participation’): http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/1069/oj.
